title: Enterprise Onboarding 1 Comprehensive Playbook (Integration, QBR, Escalation)
author: Sofia Martinez
summary: This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's enterprise onboarding procedures: pre-sales - integration - go-live - QBR cadence, plus the escalation matrix and common known issues with mitigations. It is the canonical reference for CS, support, solutions engineering, and SRE teams running enterprise customers.
audience: Customer Success Managers, Solutions Engineers, Support Engineers, SREs, Account Executives, Customer Technical Contacts
scope: Applies to all enterprise customers onboarding onto Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments. Covers technical integration checklist, operational runbook for go-live, escalation/playback procedures, and QBR/health-check artifacts.
prerequisites: Assigned CSM and SE, signed contract with deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private), customer network and security contacts identified, test account and API-key provisioning completed, minimum dataset for evals provided by customer.
integration_checklist:
| Area | Requirement | Owner | Target completion |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Contract & Entitlements | Confirm account type, rate limits, reserved capacity (if Dedicated) | CSM | -7 days |
| Access & Authentication | Customer-provided IP allowlist / VPC peering configured, API keys provisioned, KMS/HSM integration scoped (if Private) | SE/Infra | -7 days |
| Data Flows & Security | Data residency, logging, PII redaction, audit log requirements captured | Security/SE | -14 days |
| Model & Prompting | Initial model selection, quantization policy, prompt templates, eval sets uploaded | SE/Applied ML | -7 days |
| Performance Baseline | Run perf harness (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec), identify SLO targets | SRE/SE | -3 days |
| Monitoring & Alerts | Dashboards created, alert thresholds configured, tracing hooks enabled | Platform/SRE | -1 day |
| Go-live Validation | Small-scale smoke test with production traffic pattern | CSM/SE/SRE | 0 day |
onboarding_runbook:
1) Kickoff (Week -3 to -2):
- Participants: CSM (owner), SE, customer engineering, security.
- Deliverables: project plan, roles & RACI, timeline, success criteria (SLAs, latency p95 target, throughput).
2) Access & Network (Week -2):
- For Hosted: ensure IP ranges and API keys.
- For Dedicated/Private: complete VPC peering, route tables, firewall rules, and KMS integration.
3) Model Onboarding & Eval (Week -2 to -1):
- Run eval harness using customer prompts. Record quality metrics and regression baselines.
- If quantization required, coordinate with Applied ML for recommended profile.
4) Performance & Load Tests (Week -1):
- Execute benchmarking suite: steady throughput, burst, cold-cache and KV-cache warm runs. Capture p50/p95/p99 latencies and token costs.
5) Observability & Alerts (Week -1 to 0):
- Create dashboards: per-route latency, request rate, error-rate, token cost. Set alerts: error-rate > 1% sustained 5m, p95 latency > SLA +15%, disk/GPU memory > 85%.
6) Pre-Go-Live Smoke (Day 0):
- Run smoke tests: 1000 sample requests, failure rate <0.5%, end-to-end latency within SLA.
7) Go-Live (Day 0):
- Incremental rollout: route 10% - 25% - 50% - 100% traffic in 15-30 minute intervals; monitor dashboards and rollback if errors spike.
8) Stabilization (Day 1-7):
- Daily check-ins (CSM/SE/SRE). Address performance regressions, model quality issues, and billing/usage anomalies.
escalation_playbook_summary: Purpose: Provide a clear, time-bounded escalation path for incidents impacting enterprise customers (availability, data integrity, security, severe performance regressions). Use this playbook for P1/P2 incidents; P3/P4 follow standard support queues.
escalation_matrix:
| Severity | Impact | SLA | Primary contact | Secondary contact | Pager |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| P1 (Critical) | Customer outage, >50% users affected, data loss / security breach | 1 hour | SRE on-call (team-sre) | Eng Platform Lead | Yes |
| P2 (High) | Significant degradation, core features broken for some customers | 4 hours | SE on-call + CSM | Runtime Eng lead | Yes |
| P3 (Medium) | Degraded functionality, workarounds exist | 24 hours | Support queue | CSM | No |
| P4 (Low) | Minor bug, request for enhancement | N/A | Support queue | Product manager | No |
escalation_steps:
1) Triage (0-15 minutes): Confirm scope, impact, and assign severity. Notify CSM and customer technical contact.
2) Contain (15-60 minutes): If security incident, isolate affected systems (revoke keys, remove routes). If performance, enable fallback model or route to Hosted fallback pool.
3) Mitigate (60-240 minutes): Apply hotfix or rollback to last-known-good model/configuration. For infra issues, scale capacity (burst or additional node pool) and adjust batching.
4) Communicate (ongoing): Post an initial incident update within 30 minutes, then cadence every 60 minutes for P1 until resolution. Use incident template in appendix.
5) Postmortem (within 72 hours): Owner creates postmortem with timeline, root cause, and action items. Link to oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems.
known_issues_and_workarounds:
1) Intermittent 504s for long-generation requests:
- Symptom: p95 latency spikes and 504 gateway errors during >60s generation workloads.
- Workaround: Reduce max_tokens or switch to streaming responses. Increase request_timeout on client's side to 120s. Configure route-level chunked streaming.
2) High token cost after model switch:
- Symptom: Sudden increase in tokens billed following model upgrade.
- Root cause: Prompt templates not optimized for new model; sampling/temp defaults changed.
- Workaround: Revert to previous model or apply prompt truncation + token limits; open change request to Applied ML for quantization profile.
3) KV cache warming delays on Dedicated pools:
- Symptom: Cold-cache latency on first requests after scale-up.
- Workaround: Pre-warm cache using representative prompt set; enable persistent worker pools for critical routes.
4) Audit log gaps for Private deployments behind strict network ACLs:
- Symptom: Missing entries in central audit stream.
- Workaround: Confirm outbound syslog/HTTPS endpoints allowed; provide fallback S3 export for logs during maintenance windows.
support_process:
Channels: Support portal (primary), email (support@redwood.ai), in-app chat (for hosted), and phone for enterprise P1s.
Routing: Use customers' configured priority and entitlement; Dedicated customers go to priority queue (SLA-backed).
SLAs:
- P1: initial response 1 hour, resolution target 8 hours (depends on impact).
- P2: initial response 4 hours, resolution target 48 hours.
- P3: initial response 24 hours, resolution target 7 days.
- Billing/Usage inquiries: initial response 24 hours.
Escalation triggers: repeated failed deployments (3 attempts), sustained error-rate >1% for 30 minutes, security indicators, or customer executive escalation.
RCA and refunds: Post-incident RCA required for P1 outages; compensation evaluated per contract and requires finance/legal review.
health_checks_and_qbr_materials:
Standard weekly health check (owner: CSM):
- Checklist: active incidents, error-rate past 7 days, average latency (p50/p95), token consumption by route, cost anomalies, deployment changes, open action items.
- Dashboard links: per-customer route dashboard, cost breakdown (tokens, infra), model-quality drift chart.
QBR cadence: Quarterly (owner: CSM + Solutions Eng + Customer Exec Sponsor)
- Suggested agenda:
  1) Executive summary: adoption, business outcomes, top 3 wins/risks.
  2) Usage & cost trends: tokens/month, per-route costs, cost optimization opportunities.
  3) Performance & reliability: SLO attainment, incident review since last QBR.
  4) Model quality & Evals: prompt regression tests, A/B results, recommended model changes.
  5) Roadmap alignment: upcoming features (Dedicated capacity changes, Private deployment upgrades, Optimize tool updates) and migration plans.
  6) Action items & owners.
- Artifacts to prepare: usage CSV, top 10 prompts by traffic, eval baseline vs current, incident timeline.
operational_metrics_and_alerts:
Key metrics to monitor:
- Requests per second (RPS) per route.
- Token usage (inbound + outbound) per model.
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) per route - alert if > 1% sustained for 5m.
- Latency p50/p95/p99 per model/route - alert if p95 > SLA * 1.15 for 10m.
- GPU utilization and queue length - alert if GPU util > 90% or queue > 50 requests.
Recommended alert thresholds: see integration_checklist table for defaults and tune per customer SLA.
qbr_templates_and_artifacts: Attachable templates: kickoff-agenda.md, qbr-presentation-template.pptx, usage-export.csv, eval-results.csv. Use the following filenames when uploading to the customer folder: QBR-{YYYY}-Usage.csv, QBR-{YYYY}-EvalResults.csv.
post_onboarding_transition:
7-30 days after go-live: transition plan from SE to BAU support.
- Deliverables: knowledge transfer session, runbook handoff, escalation contacts updated, SLO dashboard ownership assigned.
- CSM closes onboarding after acceptance criteria met and customer signs off on 30-day stability check.
appendix:
Appendix A - Onboarding kickoff agenda:
- 0-15m: Introductions, success criteria, timeline.
- 15-30m: Security/network requirements review.
- 30-45m: Integration plan and ownership.
- 45-60m: Next steps and action items.

Appendix B - Postmortem checklist:
- Timeline with timestamps, impact statement, root cause, mitigation, remediation, preventive actions, owners, and due dates.

notes: Keep this playbook up to date after each enterprise onboarding or P1 postmortem. For major changes (process or SLA), notify stakeholders and record reviewers in this doc. If a customer requires restricted confidentiality, move a copy to restricted storage and set confidentiality to 'restricted'.
